title: Locality, Probability and the Relevance of History
version: arXiv:2610.41944v1 [quant-ph], submitted 2026-10-30, single author, University of Vienna; native arXiv HTML fetched and read through section IX (fetch truncated at ~90k chars; tail after the time-symmetry section unread).
locators: Definition 3 probabilistic world-theories, measures on initial-surface equivalence classes
Principle 2 Probabilistic Locality (dyadic supervenience of distributions)
Proposition 2 logical independence, each direction by toy example
Principle 4 Irrelevance of History with translation clause T_Sigma
Proposition 3 PL and IH jointly imply Local Causality, proof via Eqs. (13)-(17)
Sections VII-VIII red-cube toy and coherence of history relevance, Eqs. (15)-(18), footnote 12
assumptions: Globally hyperbolic Lorentzian background with Cauchy foliation; events as mutually exclusive event-types; probabilities over worlds conditioned on complete events at an initial surface Sigma_t0; footnote 9 places the spacelike event on one equal-time slice with the screen; settings independence enters only when inequalities are derived from Local Causality.
conclusion: Author's claim: relativity supports Probabilistic Locality, not Bell's Local Causality; Bell violations show history is relevant (IH false), and no tension with relativity, locality, statistical independence or realism.
proof_status: All statements and the Prop. 3 derivation steps (13)-(17) read line by line; proofs are sketch-level, not formalised; continuum and discreteness assumptions flagged by the author as innocuous simplifications.
open_questions: Does Proposition 3 survive dropping the translation clause (inherited from markov-horvat record)?
Is Probabilistic Locality defensible for theories whose state space is history-dependent?
relevance: The paper this task verifies at source; source of the conjunction result (T).
limits: Tail of section IX and any concluding section unread; author's framework never mentions temporal ontology or B&I; no concrete quantum theory is constructed (author says so).

title: Can Bohmian mechanics be made relativistic?
